Eric Mulder

Libertarian candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Colorado · Open seat

U.S. Army veteran, small business owner and security guard

Eric Mulder, of Aurora, is the Libertarian Party nominee for Governor of Colorado in the November 3, 2026 general election. His running mate for Lieutenant Governor is Wayne Harlos. He served in the U.S. Army, including in Afghanistan as a chaplain's assistant, and ran as a Libertarian for U.S. House District 6 in 2022 and Colorado House District 36 in 2024.

Where Mulder stands

Housing and cost of living
Supports more housing options, including accessory dwelling units, mobile homes and tiny-home communities. Prefers stronger tenant protections and junk-fee laws over limits on corporate ownership of single-family homes.
Homelessness
Supports decriminalizing most acts associated with homelessness and expanding tiny-home communities so people have a safe place to live and keep their belongings.
Labor Peace Act / unions
Supports workers forming unions and bargaining collectively, and would let municipalities set their own wage standards.
State budget / taxes (rural relief)
Proposes a one-year exemption from the 2.9% state sales tax for economically distressed cities and counties. Local voters could approve a temporary replacement tax for local needs.
TABOR and state budget
In a 2024 candidate survey, said TABOR needs reform that keeps voters' right to approve tax increases while cutting back or removing unnecessary restrictions.
Energy and environment
Supports expanding nuclear power to address Colorado's energy supply and affordability.
Technology regulation / surveillance
Says Flock license-plate camera systems raise serious Fourth Amendment concerns. Would oppose any expansion or unrestricted use of them.
Government accountability / antitrust
Says the Attorney General should closely monitor mergers and other antitrust concerns.
Size of government
Supports small, efficient government that uses tax dollars wisely, with solutions tailored to different regions of the state.

Background

  • U.S. Army, Specialist, 2010–2016; served in Afghanistan as a chaplain's assistant
  • BFA in Animation, Rocky Mountain College of Art + Design, 2020
  • Member, City of Aurora Veterans Affairs Commission, 2017–2019; later served on Aurora's Civic Engagement Commission
  • Former vice chair, Libertarian Party of Colorado
  • Libertarian candidate for U.S. House, Colorado District 6, 2022
  • Libertarian candidate for Colorado House District 36, 2024
  • Libertarian candidate for Arapahoe County Sheriff (Ballotpedia record)
  • Libertarian nominee for Governor of Colorado, 2026
